# Cost of Renting a Room in Toronto (2026 Budget Guide)

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/cost-of-renting-a-room-in-toronto/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-11-03

What's the cost of renting a room in Toronto in 2026? Typical ranges for rooms, studios and one-bedrooms, what's included, upfront costs and ways to pay less.

In 2026, renting a room in Toronto costs roughly $1,150 to $1,220 a month on average, according to figures compiled by the University of Toronto, while a one-bedroom apartment listed for rent typically runs about $1,900 to $2,300 or more. Downtown rooms, rooms with a private bathroom and furnished rooms usually cost more. Your real monthly cost also depends on what's included, so budget for utilities, internet and tenant insurance, not just the advertised rent.

## Key takeaways

- **Average room:** about $1,150 to $1,220 a month (City of Toronto data and U of T's Off-Campus Housing Finder listings, compiled by U of T Student Life in spring 2026).
- **Average one-bedroom:** about $1,760 for existing purpose-built rentals (CMHC) versus roughly $1,940 to $2,270 for new listings and leases (U of T Housing Finder; TRREB Q2 2026).
- **Asking rents have eased** over the past two years, according to Rentals.ca and Urbanation, but Toronto is still one of Canada's priciest rental markets.
- **Upfront, expect first month's rent plus a last month's rent deposit.** Damage deposits are not allowed in Ontario.
- **Sharing a larger unit, renting a whole home as a group, or living a few stops further out** are the most reliable ways to pay less.

## Why rent numbers don't agree

You'll see very different "average rent" figures online. That's mostly because they measure different things:

- **CMHC's Rental Market Report** surveys purpose-built rental buildings and reflects what sitting tenants pay, including people who moved in years ago and benefit from rent control. These averages run lower.
- **Listing-based reports**, like the Rentals.ca and Urbanation National Rent Report or U of T's Housing Finder, track asking rents on units available now. That's closer to what you'll pay as a new renter.
- **TRREB's rental report** tracks condo apartments leased through the MLS system across the GTA.

As a newcomer, student or anyone moving, use the listing-based figures for planning, and treat the CMHC numbers as a floor.

## Typical monthly rents in Toronto

These are averages, not quotes. Prices vary a lot by neighbourhood, building age and season.

| Type of home | Typical average | Source and notes |
|---|---|---|
| Room in a shared home | About $1,150–$1,220 | City of Toronto data and U of T Housing Finder listings (U of T Student Life, 2026) |
| Bachelor / studio | About $1,490–$1,810 | CMHC and City figures at the low end, Housing Finder listings at the high end |
| One-bedroom | About $1,760–$2,270 | CMHC purpose-built average at the low end; TRREB Q2 2026 average condo lease at the high end |
| Two-bedroom | About $2,050–$2,690 | CMHC and City figures at the low end, Housing Finder listings at the high end |
| All unit types, asking rent | About $2,500 | Rentals.ca and Urbanation, Toronto average for December 2025 |

Notice the two-bedroom row: split two ways, a two-bedroom often costs about $1,025 to $1,350 per person, close to the price of a single room but usually with more space and a shared living room.

## What's included (and what isn't)

Two listings at the same price can cost very different amounts once you add the extras. Ask about each of these before you apply:

- **Utilities.** Heat, hydro (electricity) and water. Room rentals in houses often include all three. Condos and apartments may include heat and water but bill hydro separately.
- **Internet.** Frequently included in room rentals, rarely in whole-unit rentals.
- **Laundry.** In-suite, shared in the building (often coin or card-operated) or none at all.
- **Furniture.** Furnished rooms are convenient for students and newcomers but usually cost more.
- **Parking and storage.** Often extra in condos.
- **Tenant insurance.** Many landlords ask you to carry it, and it protects your belongings and covers liability. Get quotes before you move in.
- **Transit.** If a cheaper room adds a long bus ride, add the cost of transit and your time to the comparison.

## Upfront costs to plan for

In Ontario, a landlord can collect a rent deposit of no more than one month's rent, and it must be used for your last month. They can also ask for a refundable key deposit. Damage deposits and pet deposits are not permitted. Each year, the landlord owes you interest on the last month's rent deposit at the rent increase guideline rate, which is 2.1% for 2026. Our guide to [rent deposit rules in Ontario](/blog/rent-deposit-rules-ontario/) covers the details.

So on move-in day you'll usually need:

- First month's rent
- Last month's rent deposit
- Refundable key deposit, if any
- Moving costs, basic furniture and household items
- First month of any utilities or internet in your name

## Room vs one-bedroom vs shared apartment

Each option suits a different stage of life:

- **A room in a shared house or apartment** is the cheapest way in. You share the kitchen, often a bathroom, and the common spaces. It's ideal for students, newcomers and anyone saving hard, but your comfort depends heavily on who you live with.
- **A one-bedroom or studio** gives you full privacy and control, at roughly double the cost of an average room. It makes sense if you work from home a lot, keep unusual hours or simply value your own space above savings.
- **Sharing a whole two- or three-bedroom unit** with people you choose sits in the middle. Per person, it often costs about the same as a room, but you pick your roommates and usually sign the lease together.

One more thing to check with any room rental: if you'll share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner or the owner's close family, Ontario's Residential Tenancies Act generally doesn't apply, and you'll have fewer protections. Ask who else lives there before you sign.

## How to budget for a room

A common starting point is CMHC's benchmark: housing is considered affordable when it costs less than 30% of before-tax household income. For many people in Toronto, especially students, that's out of reach for a solo apartment, which is why sharing is so common.

A simple monthly worksheet:

1. Rent (your share)
2. Utilities and internet not included in rent (your share)
3. Tenant insurance
4. Transit or commuting costs
5. Groceries and household supplies
6. A small buffer for surprises

Landlords in Ontario may ask about income, but the Ontario Human Rights Commission says income information should be considered alongside other details, such as rental history and references, not used alone as a strict cut-off.

## Ways to pay less

### Share with roommates

Splitting a two- or three-bedroom almost always beats renting alone on a per-person basis, and you usually get a living room. Use our guide to [splitting rent fairly](/blog/split-rent-fairly/) when rooms differ in size or one has a private bathroom.

### Rent a whole place as a group

### Live a few stops further out

Rents usually drop as you move away from the core. Living near a subway or LRT stop a few stations further out, such as along Line 1 in North York or Line 2 east or west, can cut rent while keeping a direct commute.

### Ask about rent control

Units first occupied before November 15, 2018 are generally covered by Ontario's annual rent increase guideline, which helps keep renewals predictable. Many newer condos are exempt, so your rent could rise more after the first year.

### Be wary of deals that look too good

A room priced far below the averages above, especially one where the "landlord" can't meet or show the place, is a classic red flag. Never pay before you've verified who you're dealing with and seen the unit.

## Compare real costs before you commit

## FAQ

**How much is a room in Toronto per month in 2026?**
U of T's Student Life office, using City of Toronto data and its own housing listings, puts the average room at about $1,150 to $1,220 a month. Rooms downtown, near campuses or with a private bathroom often cost more, and rooms further out can cost less.

**Is it cheaper to rent a room or a one-bedroom in Toronto?**
A room is almost always cheaper. Average one-bedroom rents for new listings are roughly $1,900 to $2,300 a month depending on the source, while the average room is closer to $1,200. Splitting a two-bedroom with one roommate often lands in between.

**Are utilities usually included in a Toronto room rental?**
Often, but not always. Room rentals in shared houses frequently include heat, hydro, water and internet, while condo and apartment rentals may include some utilities but charge hydro or internet separately. Always confirm in writing what the rent covers.

**What upfront costs should I expect when renting in Ontario?**
Typically your first month's rent and a rent deposit of up to one month's rent, which is applied to your last month. A landlord may also take a refundable key deposit. Damage deposits are not allowed in Ontario, so budget for moving costs and basic furniture instead.

**How much income do I need to rent in Toronto?**
CMHC treats housing as affordable when it costs under 30% of before-tax income, which is a helpful planning target. Landlords in Ontario may ask about income, but the Ontario Human Rights Commission says rigid rent-to-income cut-offs can be discriminatory, and income should be considered together with other information.

## Sources

- [UofT Student Life: Rental costs in Toronto/GTA (CMHC, City of Toronto and Housing Finder averages)](https://www.studentlife.utoronto.ca/task/rental-costs-in-toronto-gta/)
- [TRREB: Rental market report, Q2 2026](https://public.trreb.ca/wp-content/files/market-stats/rental-reports/rental_report_Q2-2026.pdf)
- [Rentals.ca and Urbanation: National Rent Report](https://rentals.ca/national-rent-report)
- [CTV News: Average rent in Toronto at its lowest since early 2022 (Rentals.ca/Urbanation data)](https://www.ctvnews.ca/toronto/article/average-rent-in-toronto-is-at-its-lowest-since-early-2022-a-new-report-finds/)
- [CMHC: Rental market reports](https://www.cmhc-schl.gc.ca/professionals/housing-markets-data-and-research/market-reports/rental-market-reports-major-centres)
- [CMHC: National Housing Strategy glossary (affordability)](https://www.cmhc-schl.gc.ca/nhs/guidepage-strategy/glossary)
- [Government of Ontario: Renting in Ontario, your rights](https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights)
- [Government of Ontario: Residential rent increases](https://www.ontario.ca/page/residential-rent-increases)
- [Ontario Human Rights Commission: Housing as a human right (newcomers)](https://www.ohrc.on.ca/en/learning/human-rights-and-newcomers/housing-human-right)

# 多伦多租房多少钱？2026 房间与公寓价格指南

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/cost-of-renting-a-room-in-toronto/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-11-03

多伦多租房多少钱？2026 年单间、studio、一室公寓的大致租金区间，房租包含哪些费用、入住前要准备多少钱，以及合租、组队整租等实用省钱办法。

多伦多租房多少钱？先给结论：根据多伦多大学 (U of T) 汇总的数据，2026 年多伦多**一个房间的平均月租大约在 1,150 到 1,220 加元**；**新出租的一室公寓平均大约 1,900 到 2,300 加元甚至更高**。市中心、带独立卫生间、带家具的房间通常更贵。另外，真正每个月要花的钱还取决于房租包含什么，水电、网费、租客保险都要算进去，不能只看广告上的那个数字。

## 先看重点

- **单间平均**：约 1,150 至 1,220 加元/月（多大学生生活办公室 2026 年春季汇总，数据来自多伦多市政府和多大校外租房平台）。
- **一室公寓平均**：CMHC 统计的老租客实际租金约 1,760 加元；新挂牌或新签约的大约 1,940 至 2,270 加元（多大房源平台、TRREB 2026 年第二季度报告）。
- **挂牌租金这两年有所回落**（Rentals.ca 与 Urbanation 数据），但多伦多仍是全加最贵的租房市场之一。
- **入住前通常要付第一个月房租和最后一个月房租押金**，安省不允许收损坏押金。
- **最有效的省钱方法**：合租大户型、组队整租、沿地铁线往外住几站。

## 为什么网上的平均租金差这么多？

你在网上会看到各种"平均房租"，数字差得很远，主要是因为统计口径不同：

- **CMHC 的租赁市场报告**调查的是专门用于出租的公寓楼，反映的是现有租客实际在付的租金，包括住了很多年、受涨租上限保护的老租客，所以数字偏低。
- **按挂牌房源统计的报告**，比如 Rentals.ca 与 Urbanation 的全国租金报告、多大校外租房平台的数据，看的是现在市场上正在出租的房子，更接近你作为新租客要付的价格。
- **TRREB（多伦多地区地产局）的租赁报告**统计的是大多伦多地区通过 MLS 系统出租的公寓。

所以，刚来多伦多的留学生和新移民做预算时，建议参考挂牌价格，把 CMHC 的数字当作"最低参考线"。

## 多伦多常见房型的大致租金

以下是平均水平，不是报价，具体价格会因社区、楼龄和季节差别很大。

| 房型 | 大致平均月租 | 数据来源与说明 |
|---|---|---|
| 合租单间 | 约 1,150–1,220 加元 | 多伦多市政府数据、多大校外租房平台（多大学生生活办公室，2026） |
| Studio / 开间 | 约 1,490–1,810 加元 | 低端为 CMHC 和市政府数据，高端为多大平台挂牌价 |
| 一室公寓 | 约 1,760–2,270 加元 | 低端为 CMHC 出租公寓平均，高端为 TRREB 2026 年第二季度平均签约价 |
| 两室公寓 | 约 2,050–2,690 加元 | 低端为 CMHC 和市政府数据，高端为多大平台挂牌价 |
| 所有房型挂牌均价 | 约 2,500 加元 | Rentals.ca 与 Urbanation，多伦多 2025 年 12 月平均 |

注意两室这一行：两个人平分，人均大约 1,025 到 1,350 加元，和租一个单间差不多，但往往空间更大，还有客厅可以用。

## 房租里包含什么？

同样价格的两个房源，加上各种额外费用后可能差很多。申请之前把下面这些问清楚：

- **水电暖**：暖气、电费 (hydro)、水费。独立屋里的合租房间常常全包；公寓楼可能包暖气和水，电费单独交。
- **网络**：合租房间经常包网，整租单位一般不包。
- **洗衣**：室内洗衣机、楼里的公共洗衣房（常常要投币或刷卡），还是根本没有。
- **家具**：带家具的房间对刚落地的人很方便，但一般更贵。
- **车位和储物间**：公寓楼里常常要另外收费。
- **租客保险**：很多房东会要求你买，它保障你的个人物品，也包含个人责任险。搬进去之前先比较几家报价。
- **交通**：便宜的房间如果每天要多坐很久的公交，把车费和时间也算进去再比较。

## 入住前要准备多少钱？

在安省，房东最多只能收**一个月房租**作为租金押金，而且这笔钱只能用来抵最后一个月的房租；另外可以收**可退还的钥匙押金**。损坏押金、宠物押金都是不允许的。房东每年还要按当年的涨租指导线给你算押金利息，2026 年是 2.1%。具体规则见 [安省押金规则](/zh/blog/rent-deposit-rules-ontario/)。

所以搬家前通常要准备：

- 第一个月房租；
- 最后一个月房租押金；
- 钥匙押金（如有，可退）；
- 搬家费、基本家具和日用品；
- 如果水电网要自己开户，第一个月的相关费用。

## 单间、整租、合租怎么选？

- **合租单间**：入门成本最低，厨房、客厅，有时还有卫生间要和别人共用。适合留学生、刚落地的新移民和想多存钱的人，但住得舒不舒服很大程度取决于室友。
- **一室公寓或 studio**：隐私和自由度最高，但价格大约是平均单间的两倍。适合经常在家办公、作息特殊，或者更看重个人空间的人。
- **和自己选的人一起整租两室、三室**：介于两者之间，人均价格常常和单间差不多，但室友是你自己挑的，通常大家一起签租约。

还有一点要特别注意：如果你要和**房屋业主本人或其近亲**共用厨房或卫生间，安省《住宅租赁法》(RTA) 一般不适用，你能享受的租客保护会少很多。签约前问清楚房子里还住着谁。

## 怎么做租房预算？

可以先参考 CMHC 的标准：住房支出低于税前收入的 30% 算可负担。对很多在多伦多的留学生和刚工作的新移民来说，一个人租公寓很难做到，这也是为什么合租如此普遍。

一个简单的月度预算清单：

1. 房租（你分摊的部分）；
2. 房租不包含的水电和网费（你分摊的部分）；
3. 租客保险；
4. 交通费；
5. 买菜和日用品；
6. 一小笔应急备用金。

房东可以了解你的收入情况，但安省人权委员会 (OHRC) 指出，收入信息应该和租房记录、推荐信等一起考虑，不能只用死板的"房租不得超过收入某个比例"来拒绝租客。

## 省钱的几个办法

### 找室友合租

按人均算，合租两室或三室几乎总比一个人住划算，而且通常有客厅。如果几个房间大小不一样、有的带独立卫生间，可以参考 [如何公平分摊房租](/zh/blog/split-rent-fairly/)。

### 组队整租

### 沿地铁线往外住几站

离市中心越远，房租一般越便宜。选择离地铁或轻轨站近、但往外多几站的地方，比如北约克 (North York) 的 1 号线沿线，或者 2 号线东西两端，既能省房租，又保留直达的通勤。看房时按上课或上班的时间实际坐一趟，确认单程时间自己能长期接受，再决定是否为了省钱住远一点。

### 问清楚是否受涨租上限保护

2018 年 11 月 15 日之前首次入住的单位，一般受安省每年涨租指导线的限制，续租时涨幅可控；很多新公寓不受限制，第一年之后房租可能涨得更多。

### 警惕"便宜得不正常"的房源

在微信群、小红书、51.ca 或约克论坛上看到价格远低于上面平均水平的房间，尤其是"房东"不能见面、不能看房、只催你先转定金的，基本可以判定是诈骗。核实对方身份、看过房子之前，一分钱都不要付。

## 留学生和新移民容易忽略的隐藏成本

除了房租和押金，刚到多伦多的人还常常低估下面几笔开销：

- **过渡住宿**：很多人落地后先住两三周短租或酒店，再实地看房。这段时间的住宿费往往比正常房租贵，要提前留出预算。
- **家具和日用品**：不带家具的房间，床垫、书桌、椅子、锅碗瓢盆加起来是一笔不小的钱。可以留意二手平台和同学毕业时转让的家具，但见面交易要注意安全。
- **开户和设备**：自己开电费、网络账户时，有的服务商要求押金或安装费；冬天如果房子保温差，电费和暖气费也可能明显上涨。
- **冬季通勤**：住得远、走路到车站要十几分钟的地方，冬天下雪时体验会差很多，有人因此不得不多花打车钱。
- **提前解约的代价**：签了一年租约，中途想搬走，一般需要找人转租或转让，或者和房东协商，否则可能要继续承担房租。签约前想清楚自己会住多久。

把这些都算进去，你会发现"便宜一两百块但条件差很多"的房子不一定真的省钱。

## 用真实成本做比较

## 常见问题

**2026 年多伦多租一个房间大概多少钱？**
根据多大学生生活办公室汇总的多伦多市政府数据和校外租房平台房源，多伦多一个房间的平均月租大约在 1,150 到 1,220 加元。市中心、靠近学校、带独立卫生间或带家具的房间通常更贵，离市中心远一些的会便宜一些。

**租单间和租一室公寓差多少？**
差距不小。新出租的一室公寓，按不同数据来源，平均大约在 1,900 到 2,300 加元之间，而单间平均在 1,200 加元左右。和一个室友合租两室公寓，人均价格通常介于两者之间。

**多伦多房租一般包水电网吗？**
要看房源类型。独立屋里的合租房间常常包暖气、电、水和网络；公寓楼可能包部分水电，但电费或网费另算。一定要在租约里写清楚房租包含哪些费用。

**在安省租房，入住前要准备多少钱？**
通常是第一个月房租，加上最多一个月房租的押金（用来抵最后一个月房租），房东还可以收可退还的钥匙押金。安省不允许收损坏押金，另外要预留搬家和买家具的钱。

**收入多少才能在多伦多租房？**
CMHC 把住房支出低于税前收入 30% 视为可负担，可以作为预算参考。房东可以了解你的收入，但安省人权委员会指出，不能只用死板的房租收入比来筛人，收入要和租房记录、推荐信等信息一起考虑。

## 参考资料

# N9 Form Ontario: How to End Your Tenancy the Right Way

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/ending-a-tenancy-n9/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-11-03

N9 form Ontario guide: 60 days' notice, ending on the last day of a rental period, fixed-term leases, roommates leaving, assignment and using your deposit.

To end a tenancy in Ontario, give your landlord **Form N9 (Tenant's Notice to End the Tenancy)** at least **60 days** before your move-out date, and make that date the **last day of a rental period** (for example, the 31st if rent is due on the 1st). If you're in a fixed-term lease, the date can't be earlier than the last day of the term. Weekly or daily tenants need 28 days, and mailing the notice adds 5 days.

Below: the exact timelines, special cases like February moves and roommates leaving, and what to do when you need out of a lease early.

## Key takeaways

- **Use Form N9** from the Landlord and Tenant Board (LTB) website. A text saying "I'm moving out" is risky.
- **60 days' notice** for monthly and fixed-term tenancies; **28 days** for weekly or daily.
- **The date must be the last day of a rental period.** In a fixed term, it can't be before the term ends.
- **Mailing?** Add 5 days.
- **Leaving mid-lease?** Agree with your landlord (N11), assign the lease, or sublet.
- **Roommates:** one co-tenant's notice generally doesn't end the tenancy for everyone.
- **Your last month's rent deposit** covers your final month.

*This is general information, not legal advice. For your situation, contact the [Landlord and Tenant Board](https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/) or a community legal clinic through Legal Aid Ontario or Steps to Justice.*

## How much notice do you need?

| Your situation | Minimum notice | Termination date |
|---|---|---|
| Month-to-month tenancy | 60 days | Last day of a rental period |
| Fixed-term lease (e.g. one year) | 60 days | No earlier than the last day of the term |
| Weekly or daily tenancy | 28 days | Last day of a rental period |
| Moving out February 28/29 | Notice by January 1 | Last day of February |
| Moving out March 31 | Notice by February 1 | March 31 |
| Landlord gave you an N12 or N13 | 10 days | Any date at least 10 days after your notice, before the landlord's date |
| Landlord refused, or didn't respond to, your request to assign | 30 days | Notice must be given within 30 days of your request |
| Landlord didn't provide the Standard Lease within 21 days of your written request | 60 days | Last day of a rental period, even during a fixed term |

If you **mail** your N9, add 5 days to these periods (for example, 65 days instead of 60).

There's also a separate process for tenants leaving because of domestic or sexual violence or abuse: **Form N15**, with 28 days' notice and supporting documents. A legal clinic or the LTB can help with that form.

## Working out your date: examples

### Rent due on the 1st

You want to move out on **June 30, 2027**.

- Hand-delivered N9: deliver by **May 1, 2027** (60 days before).
- Mailed N9: mail by **April 26, 2027** (65 days before).

### Rent due on the 15th

Your rental period runs from the 15th to the 14th. To leave in summer, your termination date would be something like **August 14**, not August 31. Give your N9 at least 60 days before August 14.

### End of a one-year lease

Your lease runs September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2027. To leave when it ends, deliver your N9 by **July 2, 2027**. If you don't give notice, your tenancy simply continues month to month; you don't need to sign a new lease to stay.

## How to fill out and deliver the N9

1. **Download the current N9** from the LTB's forms page. Forms are updated from time to time, including in 2026.
2. **Fill in** the landlord's name, every tenant's name, the rental unit address and your termination date.
3. **Sign it.** If there's more than one tenant on the lease and you're all leaving, everyone should sign.
4. **Deliver it** by handing it to your landlord, leaving it at the landlord's address in the way the rules allow, or mailing it (add 5 days). Use email only if the landlord agreed in writing to receive notices that way; many Standard Leases cover this in Section 3.
5. **Keep proof:** a photo of the signed form, the date and how you delivered it.

You don't file the N9 with the LTB; it goes to your landlord.

## After you give notice

- **Showings:** once notice is given, your landlord can show the unit to prospective tenants between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. without written notice, as long as they make a reasonable effort to let you know first.
- **Your last month:** your rent deposit covers your final rental period, so don't pay rent for that month. Make sure you've received any interest owed on it. See our guide to [last month's rent deposit rules](/blog/rent-deposit-rules-ontario/).
- **Changing your mind:** a notice you've given generally can't be cancelled on your own. If you want to stay, ask your landlord, and get their agreement in writing.
- **Not leaving on time:** if you stay past your termination date, the landlord can apply to the LTB to evict you and may claim compensation.

## Leaving a fixed-term lease early

A regular N9 can't end a fixed-term lease before its last day. Here are your realistic options:

### 1. Agree with your landlord (Form N11)

Ask whether they'll end the tenancy early. If they agree, sign an **N11 (Agreement to End the Tenancy)**. Read it carefully; once signed, you have to leave on that date.

### 2. Assign the lease

An assignment transfers your lease to a new tenant, who takes over your place and your obligations. Your landlord can:

- **Agree** to assignment in general, and then can't unreasonably refuse a specific person you propose
- **Refuse** assignment altogether, or **not respond within 7 days**, in which case you can give notice to end your tenancy within 30 days of your request

### 3. Sublet

Subletting means someone else lives in your unit for a period while you remain the tenant and plan to come back. You stay responsible to the landlord. This suits a summer away, not a permanent move.

| Option | You stay responsible? | Landlord consent needed? |
|---|---|---|
| N11 agreement | No, after the agreed date | Yes |
| Assignment | No, the new tenant takes over | Yes (and can't refuse a specific person unreasonably once they agree in principle) |
| Sublet | Yes | Yes (can't refuse unreasonably) |
| Just leaving | Possibly, for rent until a lawful end date | n/a |

If you simply move out without proper notice, you can still owe rent until the tenancy ends legally, though the landlord has a duty to make reasonable efforts to re-rent and reduce their losses. Our full guide to [sublets and assignments in Ontario](/blog/sublet-and-assignment-ontario/) walks through each step.

## When a roommate leaves

Shared leases make ending a tenancy trickier.

- **Everyone is leaving:** all co-tenants sign one N9.
- **One person is leaving:** a single co-tenant's N9 generally doesn't end the tenancy for the others. The tenancy continues for the people staying, and the person moving out may still be on the hook for rent unless the landlord agrees to take them off the lease or a replacement takes over their spot.
- **The roommate isn't on the lease:** if they rented a room from you rather than from the landlord, the arrangement is between you two. Your written house agreement should say how much notice they owe you.

The easiest fix is a written plan made before anyone moves in: notice periods between roommates, who finds the replacement, and how the departing person's share of the deposit is handled. A [roommate agreement](/blog/roommate-agreement-ontario/) is the place for that.

## Things a landlord can't make you do

- Sign an N9 at the same time you sign your lease, or as a condition of renting
- Sign an N9 or N11 because they'd like you to leave; ending your tenancy is your choice unless the LTB orders otherwise
- Forfeit your deposit or pay a "break fee" as a penalty for leaving

## Move-out checklist

- [ ] N9 delivered at least 60 days (or 65 if mailed) before the last day of a rental period
- [ ] Termination date isn't before the end of any fixed term
- [ ] Photo or copy of the signed N9 and proof of delivery
- [ ] Last month covered by your rent deposit; interest received
- [ ] Unit cleaned and photographed on move-out day
- [ ] Keys and fobs returned with written confirmation; key deposit refunded
- [ ] Forwarding address given to your landlord

## Moving on, together

## FAQ

**How much notice do I need to give my landlord in Ontario?**
For monthly and fixed-term tenancies, at least 60 days' written notice on Form N9, with the move-out date on the last day of a rental period. For daily or weekly tenancies, it's at least 28 days. Add 5 days if you mail the notice.

**Can I end a one-year lease early in Ontario?**
Not with a regular N9. In a fixed-term lease, the termination date can't be earlier than the last day of the term. Your options are to agree with the landlord to end early (Form N11), assign the lease to someone new, or sublet. If the landlord refuses to let you assign, you can give notice within 30 days of your request.

**Do I have to give notice at the end of a fixed-term lease?**
Yes, if you want to leave. A fixed-term lease doesn't end on its own; it usually continues month to month. To move out on the last day of the term, give your N9 at least 60 days before that date.

**Can my landlord make me sign an N9 when I sign the lease?**
No. A notice to end the tenancy signed at the time you enter into the lease, or as a condition of getting the lease, is generally void, with limited exceptions such as certain student residences. Signing an N9 is always your decision.

**Is there a shorter notice rule for February and March?**
Yes. If you want to move out on the last day of February, notice given by January 1 is enough. For March 31, notice given by February 1 is enough. Add extra time if you mail it.

**Does my last month's rent deposit cover my final month?**
Yes. The rent deposit must be applied to your last rent period, so if you give proper notice, you don't pay rent for that final month. Your landlord also owes any interest on the deposit.

## Sources

- [LTB Form N9: Tenant's Notice to End the Tenancy](https://tribunalsontario.ca/documents/ltb/Notices%20of%20Termination%20&%20Instructions/N9.pdf)
- [LTB Forms, filing and fees](https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/forms-filing-and-fees/)
- [Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 (Ontario e-Laws)](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17)
- [Renting in Ontario: Your rights (Government of Ontario)](https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights)
- [Steps to Justice: Figure out when to give your landlord the notice](https://stepstojustice.ca/steps/housing-law/3-figure-out-when-give-your-landlord-notice/)
- [Steps to Justice: Assign to a new tenant](https://stepstojustice.ca/steps/housing-law/assign-new-tenant/)

# 安省退租 N9 表格指南：提前60天怎么算

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/ending-a-tenancy-n9/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-11-03

安省退租 N9 表格怎么填、提前60天怎么算、固定期租约能否提前走、室友搬走怎么办、转让租约和押金抵扣，一篇讲清多伦多租客退租的完整流程和注意事项。

毕业回国、换工作、搬去和朋友合租……不管什么原因要搬家，在安省退租都有固定的规矩。**安省退租 N9** 的核心规则是：用房东与租客委员会 (LTB) 的 **N9表格**（Tenant's Notice to End the Tenancy），至少提前**60天**书面通知房东，退租日期必须是**某个租期的最后一天**（比如每月1号交租，就选月底）。固定期限租约的退租日期不能早于租期最后一天；按周或按天租的提前28天即可；邮寄通知要多加5天。

下面把时间怎么算、特殊情况和提前解约的办法一次讲清楚。

## 先看重点

- **用N9表格**，在LTB官网下载。只发一条“我要搬走了”的消息有风险。
- **按月租和固定期限：提前60天；按周/按天：提前28天。**
- **退租日必须是租期最后一天**；固定期限内不能早于到期日。
- **邮寄送达：再加5天。**
- **租期中途要走**：和房东协商 (N11)、转让租约或转租。
- **合租**：一位共同租客单独发N9，通常不会让所有人的租约一起结束。
- **最后一个月**：由租金押金抵扣。

*本文仅为一般性信息，不构成法律意见。具体情况请咨询 [房东与租客委员会 (LTB)](https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/)，或通过 Legal Aid Ontario、Steps to Justice 联系社区法律援助诊所。*

## 安省退租 N9：通知期一览

| 你的情况 | 最短通知期 | 退租日期要求 |
|---|---|---|
| 按月续租 | 60天 | 某个租期的最后一天 |
| 固定期限（如一年） | 60天 | 不早于租期最后一天 |
| 按周/按天租 | 28天 | 某个租期的最后一天 |
| 2月底搬走 | 1月1日前送达 | 2月最后一天 |
| 3月31日搬走 | 2月1日前送达 | 3月31日 |
| 房东给了你N12或N13 | 10天 | 通知后至少10天、早于房东指定日期的任意一天 |
| 房东拒绝或7天内未回复你的转让请求 | 30天 | 须在提出请求后30天内发出通知 |
| 书面要求标准租约后21天仍未提供 | 60天 | 某个租期最后一天，固定期限内也可以 |

**邮寄**N9的，以上期限都要再加5天（比如60天变成65天）。

另外，因家庭暴力或性暴力需要搬离的租客，有单独的程序：**N15表格**，提前28天，并附上相关证明文件。可以向法律诊所或LTB寻求帮助。

## 日期怎么算？举几个例子

### 每月1号交租

你想在**2027年6月30日**搬走：

- 当面送达N9：最晚**2027年5月1日**
- 邮寄N9：最晚**2027年4月26日**

### 每月15号交租

你的租期是每月15号到次月14号。暑假想搬走的话，退租日期应该是**8月14日**这样的日子，而不是8月31日。N9至少要在8月14日前60天送达。

### 一年租约到期

租约从2026年9月1日到2027年8月31日。想在到期时搬走，最晚**2027年7月2日**把N9交给房东。如果什么都不做，租约会自动转为按月续租，你想继续住也不需要签新合同。

## N9怎么填、怎么交？

1. **下载最新版N9**：到LTB官网表格页面下载，表格会不定期更新（2026年也有更新）。
2. **填写信息**：房东姓名、所有租客姓名、出租地址、退租日期。
3. **签名**：如果租约上有多位租客且都要搬走，每个人都要签。
4. **送达房东**：当面交给房东，或按规定送到房东地址，或邮寄（加5天）。只有房东书面同意用邮件接收通知时才能用邮件——很多标准租约的第3条会写明这一点。
5. **保留证据**：给签好的表格拍照，记下送达日期和方式。

N9是交给房东的，不需要提交给LTB。

### 最常见的四个填写错误

- **日期不是租期最后一天**：每月1号交租却写了15号搬走，这样的通知可能无效。
- **天数没算够**：从送达当天往后数，确认到退租日至少满60天；邮寄的再多留5天。
- **漏写室友名字**：大家都要搬走时，每位租客都要写上并签名。
- **用了旧版表格**：LTB的表格会更新，每次都从官网重新下载最保险。

## 发出N9之后

- **带人看房**：你发出通知后，房东可以在早8点到晚8点之间带潜在租客看房，不需要书面通知，但要尽量提前告诉你。
- **最后一个月**：由租金押金抵扣，这个月不用交房租。也别忘了确认押金利息是否到位，详见[安省租房押金规定](/zh/blog/rent-deposit-rules-ontario/)。
- **改变主意**：已经发出的通知，一般不能单方面撤回。想留下来，要和房东商量，并取得书面同意。
- **到期不搬**：过了退租日还不搬，房东可以向LTB申请驱逐，并可能要求赔偿。

## 一年租约没到期，想提前走怎么办？

普通N9不能在固定期限结束前终止租约。现实可行的办法有三个：

### 方法一：和房东协商（N11表格）

问问房东是否愿意提前结束租约。如果同意，双方签署 **N11表格**（Agreement to End the Tenancy）。签之前看清楚，签了就要在约定日期搬走。

### 方法二：转让租约 (Assignment)

转让是把你的租约整个交给新租客，由对方接手房子和所有义务。房东可以：

- **原则上同意转让**，之后就不能无理拒绝你推荐的具体人选
- **一概拒绝，或7天内不回复**，这时你可以在提出请求后30天内发出退租通知

### 方法三：转租 (Sublet)

转租是你暂时离开、别人住一段时间，你仍是租客、之后还会回来，你对房东的责任不变。适合暑假回国，不适合永久搬走。

| 方式 | 你还要负责吗？ | 需要房东同意吗？ |
|---|---|---|
| N11协议 | 约定日期后不用 | 需要 |
| 转让 | 不用，新租客接手 | 需要（原则上同意后不能无理拒绝具体人选） |
| 转租 | 要 | 需要（不能无理拒绝） |
| 直接搬走 | 可能要付租金到合法结束日 | — |

直接搬走、不按规定通知的话，你可能仍要承担到租约合法结束前的房租，不过房东也有义务尽合理努力重新出租、减少损失。转让和转租的完整步骤见[安省转租与转让指南](/zh/blog/sublet-and-assignment-ontario/)。

## 室友要搬走，怎么办？

合租时退租会复杂一些：

- **全部人都搬**：所有共同租客在同一份N9上签字。
- **只有一个人搬**：一位共同租客单独发N9，通常不会结束其他人的租约。留下的人继续住，搬走的人可能仍要对房租负责，除非房东同意把他从租约上移除，或有新室友接替他的位置。
- **室友不在租约上**：如果他是从你这里租的房间，而不是直接和房东签约，那就是你们两人之间的约定，提前多久通知应在你们的书面协议里写明。

最省心的办法，是入住前就把规则写下来：室友之间提前多久通知、谁负责找新室友、搬走的人那份押金怎么处理。这些都可以写进[室友协议](/zh/blog/roommate-agreement-ontario/)。

## 留学生退租的几个特别提醒

- **毕业回国别“一走了之”**：不按规定发N9就离开，可能被要求补交房租，甚至影响将来在加拿大租房的信用和推荐信。
- **算好签证和机票时间**：先确定退租日期，再倒推60天发出N9，避免机票早订、租约却还没到期。
- **留下转寄地址**：押金利息、钥匙押金退款、房东的书面确认，都需要能联系到你。可以留一个邮箱或在加拿大的朋友地址。
- **合租房提前沟通**：如果你是室友中第一个要走的，尽早告诉大家，给他们留出找新室友的时间。
- **人已经回国怎么办**：尽量在离开加拿大之前就把N9送达房东，并保存好送达凭证，人在国外再补办会麻烦很多。

## 搬走前一个月：实用时间表

| 时间点 | 要做的事 |
|---|---|
| 退租日前60天以上 | 送达N9，拍照留证；告诉室友 |
| 退租日前30–45天 | 配合房东带人看房；联系搬家公司或预约租车 |
| 退租日前2周 | 预约网络、电力等服务在退租日停止或转名 |
| 退租日前1周 | 整理物品，处理不带走的家具，避免留下垃圾 |
| 退租当天 | 打扫、拍照录像、交还钥匙和门禁卡，取得书面确认 |

提前把这些事情排进日历，退租那天就不会手忙脚乱。尤其是网络和水电，很多服务商需要提前一段时间通知才能停止，否则可能多收一个月费用。

## 房东不能逼你做的事

- 签租约时、或作为租房条件，要求你同时签N9
- 因为想让你搬走，就逼你签N9或N11——退不退租是你的决定，除非LTB另有命令
- 因为你搬走就没收押金或收“解约罚金”

## 退租检查清单

- [ ] N9在租期最后一天前至少60天（邮寄65天）送达
- [ ] 退租日期不早于固定期限的到期日
- [ ] 保留N9照片或副本，以及送达凭证
- [ ] 最后一个月由押金抵扣，利息已收到
- [ ] 搬走当天打扫干净并拍照留证
- [ ] 交还钥匙和门禁卡，取得书面确认，退回钥匙押金
- [ ] 给房东留下转寄地址

## 下一站，找对的人一起住

## 常见问题

**在安省退租需要提前多久通知房东？**
按月租和固定期限租约，需要用N9表格至少提前60天书面通知，退租日期必须是某个租期的最后一天。按周或按天租的，至少提前28天。邮寄的话要再加5天。

**签了一年的租约，可以提前退租吗？**
不能用普通N9提前结束。固定期限租约的退租日期不能早于租期最后一天。你可以和房东协商提前结束（N11表格），也可以转让 (assign) 或转租 (sublet)。如果房东拒绝你转让，你可以在提出请求后30天内发出退租通知。

**一年租约到期，我需要提前通知吗？**
需要。固定期限租约到期后不会自动结束，通常会转为按月续租。如果想在到期日搬走，要在到期日前至少60天发出N9。

**房东要求我签租约时顺便签一份N9，合法吗？**
一般不合法。在签租约时、或作为签约条件而签署的退租通知通常无效（部分学生宿舍等情况例外）。签不签N9永远是你自己的决定。

**2月和3月退租有特殊规定吗？**
有。想在2月最后一天搬走，1月1日前发出通知即可；想在3月31日搬走，2月1日前发出通知即可。邮寄的话要再预留时间。

**最后一个月的房租押金能直接抵吗？**
可以。租金押金必须用于抵扣最后一期房租，只要按规定发了退租通知，最后一个月就不用再交房租。房东还应付清押金利息。

## 参考资料

- [LTB Brochure: How a Tenant Can End Their Tenancy](https://tribunalsontario.ca/documents/ltb/Brochures/How%20a%20Tenant%20Can%20End%20Their%20Tenancy%20(EN).html)
- [LTB Form N9: Tenant's Notice to End the Tenancy](https://tribunalsontario.ca/documents/ltb/Notices%20of%20Termination%20&%20Instructions/N9.pdf)
- [LTB Forms, filing and fees](https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/forms-filing-and-fees/)
- [Residential Tenancies Act, 2006（安省法律数据库）](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17)
- [Renting in Ontario: Your rights（安省政府）](https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights)
- [Steps to Justice: Figure out when to give your landlord the notice](https://stepstojustice.ca/steps/housing-law/3-figure-out-when-give-your-landlord-notice/)
- [Steps to Justice: Assign to a new tenant](https://stepstojustice.ca/steps/housing-law/assign-new-tenant/)
- [CLEO: Moving out: Giving notice](https://www.cleo.on.ca/wp-content/uploads/notice.pdf)

# Find a Roommate in Toronto: The 2026 Guide

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/find-a-roommate-in-toronto/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-11-03

How to find a roommate in Toronto in 2026: where to look, how to vet people, red flags to avoid, what to ask when you meet and how to put it in writing.

To find a roommate in Toronto, decide your budget and must-haves first, then search two or three channels at once (matching apps, school or work networks, and trusted community groups). Shortlist people whose habits match yours, meet them by video and in person, verify identity and the listing, and put your arrangement in writing before anyone pays or moves in.

That's the short version. The rest of this guide walks through each step with the checks that keep you safe and the questions that help you pick someone you will actually enjoy living with.

## Key takeaways

- **Start early.** Four to six weeks before move-in is a comfortable runway; late summer is the most competitive time in Toronto.
- **Match on habits, not just budget.** Sleep schedule, cleanliness and guests cause more fights than money does.
- **Verify before you pay.** Confirm the person, the unit and who actually has the right to rent it.
- **Know your legal setup.** Co-tenant on the lease, roommate of a tenant, or renting from a live-in owner each give you different protections.
- **Write it down.** A one- or two-page roommate agreement prevents most disputes.

## Step 1: Get clear on what you need

Before you scroll a single listing, write down your answers to these. It makes every later conversation faster.

- **Budget:** your maximum monthly rent *plus* your share of utilities and internet. Room prices in Toronto vary widely by neighbourhood, unit type and whether you get a private bathroom, so treat any number you hear as a rough guide.
- **Location:** your commute to school or work, and how close you need to be to the TTC.
- **Move-in date and lease length:** 4, 8 or 12 months? Flexible or fixed?
- **Must-haves:** private bathroom, laundry in the unit, parking, pet-friendly.
- **Deal-breakers:** smoking, overnight partners every night, a dog, a night-shift schedule.

### Decide which type of arrangement you want

| Arrangement | What it means | What to watch |
|---|---|---|
| Co-tenants | Everyone signs the lease with the landlord | Each person is usually responsible to the landlord for the whole rent |
| Roommate of a tenant | One person holds the lease; you pay them | You may have few rights against the landlord; get a written roommate agreement |
| Room in an owner-occupied home | You rent a room from an owner who lives there | If you share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner or close family, the Residential Tenancies Act may not apply |
| Whole home rented room by room | Each person rents their own room in the same home | Check how shared costs and house rules are handled |

If you are not sure which of these applies to a room you are considering, ask the person renting it directly, and check with the Landlord and Tenant Board or a legal clinic before you sign anything.

## Step 2: Where to look for a roommate in Toronto

Use more than one channel. Each has strengths and weak spots.

- **Your school or employer.** University and college off-campus housing boards, alumni groups and workplace channels give you a built-in layer of accountability.
- **Friends and referrals.** Still one of the safest routes. Ask your network early, even people you think are unlikely to know someone.
- **Community and social media groups.** Neighbourhood, cultural and newcomer groups are busy and useful, but they are also where many fake listings appear.
- **General classifieds.** Big reach, minimal screening. Expect to do all of the verification yourself.

### Write a profile that attracts the right people

Be specific and honest. "Quiet nurse, works three 12-hour night shifts a week, tidy, no pets, occasional weekend guest" will get you better matches than "easygoing, clean, fun." Mention your budget range, target neighbourhoods and move-in date up front.

## Step 3: Shortlist and screen

Once messages start coming in, screen quickly and politely.

### First-message checklist

- [ ] They answered your actual questions rather than sending a generic reply
- [ ] Their budget and move-in date fit yours
- [ ] They're willing to do a live video call
- [ ] They didn't ask for money, ID scans or banking details at this stage

### Red flags to walk away from

- Asking for a deposit or "holding fee" before you've seen the place or signed anything
- Refusing a live video call or in-person viewing with a vague excuse
- A rent price far below everything comparable in the area
- Pressure to decide today because "lots of people are interested"
- Stories that change: a different unit, a different landlord, a different reason they're overseas
- Requests for payment by gift card, crypto or wire transfer to an individual abroad

Scams are common enough that we wrote a full guide: [Toronto rental scams and how to verify a landlord](/blog/toronto-rental-scams/).

## Step 4: The first meeting

Do a short video call first, then meet in person, ideally at the unit. Bring a list of questions. The big topics are money, cleaning, guests, noise, sleep schedules, work-from-home routines, food sharing and pets. We put together a ready-to-use list of [30 questions to ask a potential roommate](/blog/questions-to-ask-a-roommate/).

A few tips:

- **Ask for examples, not labels.** "What does clean mean to you? How often do you do dishes?" works better than "Are you clean?"
- **Share your own quirks.** It invites honesty and shows you're serious.
- **Notice how they handle disagreement.** If you differ on something small, do they listen or dismiss you?
- **Meet safely.** Pick a public place or bring a friend if you're meeting at a private home for the first time, and tell someone where you're going.

## Step 5: Verify the person and the place

This step separates a smooth move from a costly mistake.

### Verify the person

- Confirm their name matches their profile and any references.
- Ask for a reference from a previous landlord or roommate and actually call it.
- If they're a student or employee, a quick look at a school or work profile can confirm the basics.

### Verify the unit and the person renting it

- See the unit in person, or by live video if you truly can't travel, with the person walking room to room in real time.
- If an agent is involved, check that they're registered with the Real Estate Council of Ontario (RECO).
- If you're renting directly, ask who owns the unit and how the person has the right to rent it out.
- Make sure there will be a written lease. For most residential tenancies in Ontario, landlords must use the government's standard lease form.

### Know the deposit rules

In most Ontario tenancies covered by the Residential Tenancies Act, a landlord can ask for a rent deposit of no more than one month's rent (used for the last month) and a refundable key deposit, but not a separate "damage deposit." Never pay anything before you've seen the place and have a signed lease in hand.

## Step 6: Put it in writing

Once you've chosen someone, write a short roommate agreement. Cover:

- How rent is split and who pays the landlord
- How utilities and internet are divided and paid
- Chores and shared supplies
- Guests and overnight visitors
- Quiet hours
- What happens if someone wants to move out early

Our step-by-step [roommate agreement guide for Ontario](/blog/roommate-agreement-ontario/) includes a template outline you can adapt, plus tips for splitting rent when the rooms aren't equal.

## Step 7: Move in on the right foot

- **Do a move-in walkthrough** together and take dated photos of every room.
- **Set up shared bills** in a way that's easy to track.
- **Agree on a check-in.** A quick chat after the first two weeks catches small annoyances before they grow.

## Finding a roommate as a newcomer or student

If you're new to Canada, you may not have a credit history or local references yet. That's normal. Offer what you do have: a school acceptance letter, an employment letter, proof of funds or a reference from a previous landlord abroad.

Be extra careful about paying from overseas. Many scams target people who can't view a unit before arriving. If you can, book short-term accommodation for your first couple of weeks and view rooms in person.

## FAQ

**Where is the best place to find a roommate in Toronto?**
Most people use a mix of channels: roommate-matching apps, university housing boards, community groups and referrals from friends or coworkers. Matching platforms save time because you can filter by budget, schedule and habits before you ever chat. Whatever channel you use, verify the person and the listing before paying anything.

**How long does it take to find a roommate in Toronto?**
It varies a lot with the season, your budget and how flexible you are on location. Give yourself at least four to six weeks before your move-in date, and more if you are searching during the busy late-summer student season.

**Do I need a written roommate agreement in Ontario?**
It is not legally required, but it is strongly recommended. A short written agreement covering rent, bills, chores, guests and moving out prevents most disputes. It is a private agreement between roommates and does not replace the lease you have with the landlord.

**Does the Residential Tenancies Act protect me if I rent a room?**
Often, but not always. In Ontario the Act generally does not apply if you share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner or certain close family members of the owner who live there. Check your situation with the Landlord and Tenant Board or a legal clinic before you sign.

**Is it safe to find a roommate on social media or group chats?**
It can be, but scams and fake profiles are common. Meet in person or by live video, confirm identity, never pay a deposit before seeing the place and signing a lease, and be wary of anyone who pressures you to decide fast.

## Sources

- [Renting in Ontario: Your rights (Government of Ontario)](https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights)
- [Guide to Ontario's standard lease (Government of Ontario)](https://www.ontario.ca/page/guide-ontarios-standard-lease)
- [Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 (Ontario e-Laws)](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17)
- [Find out if the Residential Tenancies Act applies (Steps to Justice)](https://stepstojustice.ca/steps/housing-law/1-find-out-if-the-residential-tenancies-act-applies/)
- [Landlord and Tenant Board (Tribunals Ontario)](https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/)
- [Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre](https://antifraudcentre-centreantifraude.ca/)

# 多伦多找室友全攻略（2026版）

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/find-a-roommate-in-toronto/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-11-03

多伦多找室友怎么找才靠谱？本文从渠道选择、身份和房源核实、常见危险信号，一路讲到第一次见面要问什么、怎么签室友协议，留学生和新移民一篇就能看懂。

多伦多找室友，最稳妥的做法是：先想清楚预算和底线，再同时用两三个渠道找人；挑出生活习惯合拍的候选人，视频加当面聊过，核实对方身份和房源真实性；最后把规则写成室友协议，再付钱、再搬家。

听起来简单，但每一步都有坑。下面按顺序讲清楚，特别照顾第一次在加拿大租房的留学生和新移民。

## 先看要点

- **早点开始**：至少提前四到六周，开学季（八九月）要更早。
- **习惯比预算更重要**：作息、卫生、带朋友回家，才是室友矛盾的主要来源。
- **先核实，再付钱**：确认人是真的、房是真的、对方真的有权出租。
- **搞清楚自己的身份**：你是租约上的共同租客，还是"二房东"的室友，还是和业主同住？法律保护不一样。
- **写下来**：一两页的室友协议，能避免大多数纠纷。

## 第一步：想清楚自己要什么

在刷房源之前，先把这几件事写在手机备忘录里，后面每一次沟通都会快很多：

- **预算**：房租上限，加上你要分摊的水电、暖气和网费。多伦多单间租金因区域、房型、是否独立卫浴、是否包家具差别很大，网上看到的数字只能当粗略参考，最好多看几套同区域的房源自己对比。
- **位置**：离学校或公司多远？离地铁站、公交线近不近？冬天走路十五分钟和夏天走路十五分钟，体感完全不同。
- **入住时间和租期**：4个月、8个月还是一年？能不能灵活？很多留学生只需要一个学期，要提前和对方说清楚。
- **必须有的**：独立卫生间、室内洗衣机、停车位、可以养宠物、可以做中餐（油烟大不大是很多合租家庭真实会吵的点）。
- **绝对不能接受的**：抽烟、伴侣天天留宿、养狗、对方上夜班等。

### 合租形式有哪几种？

| 形式 | 含义 | 需要注意 |
|---|---|---|
| 共同租客 (co-tenants) | 所有人都在租约上签字 | 通常每个人都要对房东负责全部房租 |
| 租客的室友 | 只有一人签租约，你把钱交给他 | 你对房东的权利可能很有限，务必签室友协议 |
| 和业主同住 | 业主自己也住在房子里 | 如果和业主或其近亲共用厨房或卫生间，《住宅租赁法》(RTA) 可能不适用 |
| 整栋按房间分租 | 每人各租一间，同住一栋 | 问清楚公共费用和屋规怎么定 |

很多同学在微信群里租的"单间"，其实是第二种：一个人和房东签了约，再把其他房间转租出去，俗称"二房东"。这种情况下，你的押金交给谁、出了问题找谁，一定要事先问清楚。如果不确定自己属于哪一种，签约前可以咨询房东与租客委员会 (LTB) 或社区法律诊所。

## 第二步：多伦多找室友去哪里找？

不要只盯一个渠道，各有优缺点：

- **学校和公司资源**：大学的校外住房平台 (off-campus housing)、校友群、公司内部群，相对更有约束力。
- **朋友介绍**：依然是最安全的方式之一，尽早在朋友圈里问一圈，连"不太可能认识人"的朋友也问问。
- **华人社区渠道**：微信群、小红书、51.ca、约克论坛 (yorkbbs) 上合租信息非常多，更新也快，对刚落地的同学很方便。但这些地方也是假房源、冒充房东、"先转定金"骗局的高发地，后面的核实步骤一步都不能省。
- **综合分类网站**：覆盖面大，但几乎没有筛选，全部要靠自己核实。

### 怎么写一条好的找室友帖子

越具体越好。与其写"人好相处、爱干净"，不如写"护士，每周三个夜班，作息规律，不养宠物，偶尔周末有朋友来访"。把预算范围、目标区域、入住日期放在最前面，能直接过滤掉不合适的人。

在小红书或微信群发帖时，不要把学号、护照、具体门牌号、手机号直接贴出来，有意向的人私聊再说。

## 第三步：初筛候选人

消息多起来以后，要快速、礼貌地筛选。

### 初次沟通检查清单

- [ ] 对方认真回答了你的问题，而不是群发模板
- [ ] 预算和入住时间对得上
- [ ] 愿意视频通话
- [ ] 没有在这个阶段就要钱、要护照照片或银行信息

### 看到这些信号，直接放弃

- 还没看房、没签任何东西，就要你先转"定金""占位费"
- 用各种理由拒绝视频或实地看房，比如"人在国外""钥匙在中介那"
- 租金比同区域同类房源低得离谱
- 不停催你"今天必须定，好多人在抢"
- 说法前后不一致：房子换了、房东换了、理由换了
- 要求用礼品卡、加密货币，或者转账到海外个人账户

这类骗局在多伦多很常见，我们专门写了一篇：[多伦多租房诈骗识别与防范](/zh/blog/toronto-rental-scams/)。

## 第四步：第一次见面聊什么

建议先视频，再当面，最好直接约在房子里。准备好问题清单，重点聊：钱怎么分、卫生标准、访客和留宿、噪音和作息、是否在家办公、食物共享、宠物。我们整理了一份可以直接用的 [找室友要问的30个问题](/zh/blog/questions-to-ask-a-roommate/)。

几个小技巧：

- **问具体例子，别问标签**："你一般多久洗一次碗？"比"你爱干净吗？"有用得多。
- **主动说自己的小习惯**：你坦诚，对方也更愿意说实话。
- **观察对方怎么处理分歧**：小事上意见不同时，是认真听还是不耐烦？
- **注意人身安全**：第一次去陌生人家里，可以约朋友一起，或者提前告诉家人朋友你的去向。

## 第五步：核实人，也核实房

这一步决定你是顺利入住，还是钱房两空。

### 核实室友本人

- 名字和资料是否一致，有没有前任房东或室友可以做推荐人，而且真的打电话问一下。
- 如果对方说自己是学生或在某公司上班，可以简单查一下学校或职业资料是否吻合。

### 核实房源和出租人

- 实地看房；实在来不了，也要让对方实时视频带你一间一间看，打开窗户看看街景，和房源描述对得上。
- 如果有中介，到安省地产委员会 (RECO) 的官网注册查询 (Registrant Search) 里查一下中介是否注册、有没有处分记录。
- 如果是房东直租，问清楚房子是谁的，对方凭什么有权出租。如果是"二房东"，可以请他出示和房东签的租约。
- 坚持签书面租约。在安省，大多数住宅租赁都必须使用政府的标准租约 (Standard Lease)，房东要在你签字后21天内给你一份副本。

### 了解押金规则

在受《住宅租赁法》保护的大多数租约里，房东最多只能收一个月房租作为租金押金（用来抵最后一个月房租），以及可退还的钥匙押金，不能另外收"损坏押金"。记住一句话：没看过房、没签租约，一分钱都不要转。

## 第六步：签一份室友协议

选好人以后，花半小时写一份室友协议，至少包括：

- 房租怎么分，谁负责交给房东
- 水电网费怎么分、怎么付
- 家务分工和公共用品（洗洁精、卫生纸、垃圾袋谁买）
- 访客和留宿规则
- 安静时间
- 有人想提前搬走怎么办，押金怎么退

具体写法、模板和房间大小不一样时房租怎么分，都在 [安省室友协议怎么写](/zh/blog/roommate-agreement-ontario/) 里。

## 第七步：入住之后

- **一起做入住检查**：每个房间拍带日期的照片，留好证据，搬走时退押金会用到。
- **把公共账单管清楚**：用共享表格或记账软件，谁付了什么一目了然。
- **两周后聊一次**：趁小问题还没变成大矛盾，坐下来调整一下规则。
- **建一个小群**：室友之间的事在群里说，比在背后吐槽有效得多。

## 给留学生和新移民的几点提醒

刚来加拿大，没有本地信用记录、没有本地推荐人，这很正常。可以准备录取通知书、在职证明、资金证明，或者国内房东的推荐信，让对方放心。

人在国内就要付款的情况要格外谨慎，很多骗局专门针对"还没落地、没法看房"的同学。条件允许的话，先订两三周的短租，落地后再实地看房、见室友。哪怕多花一点短租费，也比提前转几千加元定金却发现房子根本不存在要好。

另外，文化习惯差异也值得提前聊：比如是否经常在家做饭、是否在家里穿鞋、空调和暖气开到多少度、会不会有家人长期来探亲。这些在国内觉得理所当然的事，在合租里往往最容易产生摩擦。

## 常见问题

**在多伦多找室友一般要提前多久？**
建议至少提前四到六周开始。如果是八九月开学季，竞争最激烈，最好再提前一些。预算越紧、对地段要求越具体，所需时间通常越长。

**在微信群或小红书上找室友安全吗？**
可以用，但要格外小心。这些渠道信息多、更新快，假房源和冒充房东的情况也不少。一定要视频或当面确认身份、实地看房，签好租约之前不要转任何定金。

**只租一个房间，受安省租客法保护吗？**
多数情况下受保护，但有例外。如果你和房屋业主本人或其特定近亲（配偶、子女、父母等）共用厨房或卫生间，《住宅租赁法》(RTA) 一般不适用。签约前最好向房东与租客委员会 (LTB) 或法律援助诊所确认。

**室友协议有法律效力吗？**
室友协议是室友之间的私人约定，不能代替你和房东签的租约，也约束不了房东。但它能把房租分摊、家务、访客、搬走等规则写清楚，发生纠纷时也是重要的书面证据。

**没有加拿大信用记录怎么找室友和租房？**
这对新移民和留学生很常见。可以提供录取通知书、在职证明、资金证明或以前房东的推荐信。如果被要求预付多个月房租，要知道这通常可以协商，付款前务必确认房源真实、租约已签。

## 参考资料

- [Renting in Ontario: Your rights（安省政府）](https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights)
- [Guide to Ontario's standard lease（安省标准租约指南）](https://www.ontario.ca/page/guide-ontarios-standard-lease)
- [Residential Tenancies Act, 2006（安省法律 e-Laws）](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17)
- [Find out if the Residential Tenancies Act applies（Steps to Justice）](https://stepstojustice.ca/steps/housing-law/1-find-out-if-the-residential-tenancies-act-applies/)
- [RECO Registrant Search（安省地产委员会注册查询）](https://registrantsearch.reco.on.ca/)
- [Landlord and Tenant Board（房东与租客委员会）](https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/)
- [Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre（加拿大反诈骗中心）](https://antifraudcentre-centreantifraude.ca/)

# International Student Housing in Toronto: 2026 Checklist

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/international-student-renting-toronto/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-11-03

International student housing in Toronto, step by step: when to start, residence vs off-campus, documents, remote viewings, the lease, deposits and scams.

International students looking for housing in Toronto should start with their school's housing office, apply for residence as soon as they accept an offer, and begin the off-campus search about one to two months before move-in, when most listings appear. Never send money for a place you haven't verified, make sure you sign Ontario's Standard Lease where it applies, and don't pay more than the deposits Ontario allows.

## Key takeaways

- **Residence deadlines come early.** At U of T, for example, first-year students had to apply through the residence portal by March 31 to keep the residence guarantee for 2026 entry.
- **Off-campus listings appear late.** Many tenants give 60 days' notice, so most units hit the market one to two months ahead.
- **Prepare documents now:** passport, study permit or letter of introduction, proof of enrolment and proof of funds.
- **Verify before you pay.** Live video tours and a trusted local contact beat any promise made over chat.
- **Know the deposit limits:** a last month's rent deposit of up to one month's rent and a refundable key deposit. No damage deposits.
- **Use your school.** Housing offices can help you check listings, leases and red flags for free.

## Your timeline at a glance

| When | What to do |
|---|---|
| As soon as you accept your offer | Check residence options and deadlines; apply if you want to live on campus |
| 3–4 months before arrival | Research neighbourhoods near your campus, set a budget, join official school housing platforms |
| 6–8 weeks before move-in | Search actively, book viewings (in person or live video), line up references and proof of funds |
| 2–4 weeks before move-in | Sign the lease, pay deposits by a traceable method, arrange tenant insurance and utilities |
| Move-in day | Inspect the unit, take dated photos, test locks and smoke alarms, and get keys and receipts |

If you can't lock in a long-term place before you fly, book a short-term stay for your first few weeks. Viewing in person after you land is the single best protection against scams.

## Residence or off-campus?

| | Residence (on campus) | Off-campus rental |
|---|---|---|
| Convenience | Steps from class, often with meal plans | Depends on your commute |
| Paperwork | Applied through your school | Application, lease and deposits with a private landlord |
| Cost | Fixed fees set by the school | Varies widely; rooms average about $1,150–$1,220 a month in Toronto |
| Flexibility | Academic-year terms, house rules | Usually 12-month leases; more independence |
| Social life | Built-in community | You choose your roommates |
| Risk of scams | Very low | Higher; verify everything |

Many international students spend their first year in residence and move off campus afterwards. If residence is full or too expensive, our guide to the [best Toronto neighbourhoods for students](/blog/best-toronto-neighbourhoods-for-students/) helps you shortlist areas near your campus.

## Documents to have ready

Keep digital copies in one folder so you can apply quickly:

- **Passport** (share a copy only once the landlord is verified)
- **Study permit**, or your port-of-entry letter of introduction if you haven't arrived yet
- **Letter of acceptance or proof of enrolment**
- **Proof of funds**: recent bank statements, scholarship letters or a sponsor's letter
- **References**: a previous landlord, a professor or an employer, if you have them
- **Guarantor information**, if a landlord asks and you have someone in Canada who can help

You don't need a Social Insurance Number to rent. Service Canada lists renting a property and filling out a rental application among situations where you don't have to provide it. If you have no Canadian credit history yet, that's normal for students: offer proof of funds, your enrolment letter and references instead, and remember that a lack of credit history shouldn't be held against you in Ontario.

## Viewing a place remotely, safely

If you're still abroad:

1. **Ask for a live video tour**, not pre-recorded clips. Ask the person to open closets, run the taps, show the view from the window and walk to the front door so you can see the street.
2. **Confirm who they are.** Ask for their full name and check that they own or manage the unit. A property management company should have a website, office address and phone number you can verify.
3. **Ask a trusted friend in Toronto** to view the unit in person if possible.
4. **Search the address and photos online.** Scammers often copy photos from real listings.
5. **Ask your school's housing office** to look at the listing and lease if anything feels off.

## Signing the Standard Lease

Most residential tenancies in Ontario must use the government's Standard Lease form. It sets out the rent, what's included, deposits and the rules both sides must follow. Read the "additional terms" section carefully, because a term that breaks the Residential Tenancies Act can't be enforced, even if you signed it.

If your landlord doesn't give you the Standard Lease, you can ask for it in writing. If they don't provide it within 21 days, Ontario's rules give you options, including withholding up to one month's rent in some circumstances. Our full guide to the [Ontario Standard Lease](/blog/ontario-standard-lease/) walks through each section.

One important exception: if you share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner or the owner's close family, the Residential Tenancies Act generally doesn't apply, and neither does the Standard Lease. That's common in homestays and some room rentals, so ask before you sign.

## Deposits and payments

In Ontario, a landlord can collect:

- A **rent deposit** of no more than one month's rent, which must be used for your last month
- A **refundable key deposit**

Damage deposits are not allowed. The landlord owes you annual interest on the rent deposit at the rent increase guideline rate (2.1% for 2026). A landlord can't make several months of prepaid rent a condition of renting to you; if you choose to offer it, do so only after verifying the landlord and signing the lease, and get a receipt.

Pay by a traceable method, such as an e-transfer to a verified landlord or a cheque, and keep every receipt and message.

## Scams that target international students

Students are targeted because they often rent from abroad, under time pressure. In June 2026, Toronto police announced an arrest in an alleged rental fraud near Yonge and Finch in which international students paid deposits for apartments they hadn't viewed. Watch for:

- **Too-good-to-be-true rent** in popular areas
- **"I'm overseas, I'll mail you the keys"** stories
- **The same unit rented to several people**, each paying a deposit
- **Fake agents** asking for passport and permit copies before any viewing
- **Pressure to pay today** because "many students are interested"
- **Sublets from someone with no right to sublet**

If you're targeted, contact your bank immediately, report to the Toronto Police Service and the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre, and tell your school's housing office. Read more in our guide to [Toronto rental scams](/blog/toronto-rental-scams/).

## Use your school's housing office

- **University of Toronto:** the Off-Campus Housing Finder is open to students with a UTORid and includes a roommate finder.
- **Toronto Metropolitan University:** the Off-Campus Housing Office offers appointments and resources for current and incoming students.
- **York University:** off-campus housing services include a listing platform and support for tenant-landlord issues.
- **Colleges** such as Humber, Seneca, Centennial and George Brown have housing or student-life teams who can help.

These services are free, and staff have seen every scam in the book.

## After you move in

A few small steps in your first week can save you a lot of trouble later:

- **Document the unit's condition.** Take dated photos and videos of every room, including any damage, and email them to your landlord so there's a record.
- **Get tenant insurance** if you haven't already. It covers your belongings and your liability if, for example, you accidentally cause a leak.
- **Set up utilities and internet** that aren't included in your rent, and confirm whose name each account is in.
- **Save your landlord's contact details** and the process for repair requests, preferably in writing.
- **Pay rent on time and keep receipts.** A clean rental record here becomes a reference for your next place.

## Find roommates you can trust

## FAQ

**When should international students start looking for housing in Toronto?**
Apply for residence as soon as you accept your offer, since deadlines can come early in the year. For off-campus rentals, most units are listed about one to two months before they're available, partly because tenants on monthly leases must give 60 days' notice to move out. Start researching neighbourhoods and budgets earlier, and search actively six to eight weeks before your move.

**Can I rent an apartment in Toronto before I arrive in Canada?**
Yes, but it's riskier. If you sign from abroad, verify the landlord's identity, get a live video tour, ask someone you trust in Toronto to view it in person, and only pay after you've signed a written lease. Many students book a short-term stay for the first few weeks and sign a long-term lease after viewing in person.

**What documents do international students need to rent in Toronto?**
Landlords usually ask for a passport, your study permit or letter of introduction, proof of enrolment, proof of funds such as bank statements, and references if you have them. Some also ask for a guarantor. You don't need to give your Social Insurance Number to rent.

**Is it safe to pay a deposit before seeing a place?**
It's one of the most common ways students lose money. Never pay before you've verified that the person owns or manages the unit and you've seen it in person or on a live video call. Pay by a traceable method and get a receipt.

**Does the Ontario Standard Lease apply if I rent a room?**
Usually yes, if the Residential Tenancies Act applies to your rental. A key exception is when you share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner or the owner's close family; then the Act and the Standard Lease generally don't apply, and you have fewer protections.

**Where can international students get help with housing in Toronto?**
Start with your school's housing office. U of T has an Off-Campus Housing Finder, TMU has an Off-Campus Housing Office, and York has off-campus housing services. Colleges also have housing or student-life staff who can review listings and leases with you.

- [UofT Student Life: Rental costs in Toronto/GTA](https://www.studentlife.utoronto.ca/task/rental-costs-in-toronto-gta/)
- [Toronto Metropolitan University: Find a place off campus](https://www.torontomu.ca/housing/housing-alternatives/off-campus/find-a-place/)
- [York University: Off-campus housing](https://www.yorku.ca/housing/off-campus-housing/)

# 多伦多留学生租房全攻略：时间线与避坑清单

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/international-student-renting-toronto/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-11-03

多伦多留学生租房完整清单：什么时候开始找、住宿舍还是校外、要准备哪些材料、人在国内怎么安全看房、标准租约和押金规定，以及专门针对留学生的骗局。

多伦多留学生租房，最重要的三件事：**先找学校住房办公室、宿舍要早申请、校外租房在入住前一到两个月集中找**。没有核实过的房子一分钱都不要付；签约尽量使用安省标准租约 (Standard Lease)；押金不要超过安省法律允许的范围。下面按时间顺序，把从拿到录取到搬进新家的每一步都列清楚。

## 先看重点

- **宿舍截止日期很早**：以多伦多大学 (U of T) 为例，2026 年入学的一年级新生要在 3 月 31 日前通过宿舍系统提交申请，才能保留宿舍保证资格。
- **校外房源出得晚**：按月租住的租客搬走要提前 60 天通知房东，所以大部分房源在入住前一到两个月才上市。
- **材料现在就准备**：护照、学签或签证批准信、在读证明、资金证明。
- **先核实、再付款**：实时视频看房、本地朋友帮忙实地看，比任何聊天记录里的承诺都可靠。
- **押金有上限**：最多一个月房租的押金（抵最后一个月）加可退还的钥匙押金，不允许收损坏押金。
- **善用学校资源**：学校住房办公室可以免费帮你看房源、看租约、识别骗局。

## 租房时间线

| 时间 | 要做的事 |
|---|---|
| 接受录取后 | 了解宿舍选项和截止日期，想住校就尽快申请 |
| 入学前 3–4 个月 | 研究学校周边社区、定预算、注册学校官方租房平台 |
| 入住前 6–8 周 | 集中找房，预约看房（实地或实时视频），准备推荐信和资金证明 |
| 入住前 2–4 周 | 签租约，用可追踪的方式付押金，办好租客保险和水电网 |
| 搬家当天 | 检查房屋、拍带日期的照片、测试门锁和烟雾报警器，拿到钥匙和收据 |

如果出发前实在定不下长租，可以先订两三周的短租。**落地后实地看房，是防骗最有效的一招。**

## 住宿舍还是校外租房？

| | 学校宿舍 | 校外租房 |
|---|---|---|
| 便利程度 | 离教室近，常配餐卡 | 取决于通勤 |
| 手续 | 通过学校申请 | 和私人房东签申请、租约、付押金 |
| 费用 | 学校统一定价 | 差别很大，多伦多单间平均约 1,150–1,220 加元/月 |
| 灵活度 | 按学年入住，有宿舍规定 | 一般签 12 个月，更自由 |
| 社交 | 自带社交圈 | 室友自己选 |
| 被骗风险 | 很低 | 较高，样样都要核实 |

很多留学生第一年住宿舍，第二年再搬出去住。如果宿舍满了或太贵，可以先看看 [多伦多留学生住哪里](/zh/blog/best-toronto-neighbourhoods-for-students/)，按校区挑社区。

## 需要准备的材料

把电子版放在同一个文件夹里，看到合适的房子可以马上申请：

- **护照**（确认房东真实后再发复印件）；
- **学签**，如果还没入境，可以先提供签证批准信 (letter of introduction)；
- **录取信或在读证明**；
- **资金证明**：近期银行流水、奖学金证明或父母的资助说明；
- **推荐信**：以前的房东、老师或雇主（有的话）；
- **担保人信息**：如果房东要求，并且你在加拿大有人可以帮忙。

租房不需要社会保险号 (SIN)。加拿大服务部把租房、填写租房申请列为不必提供 SIN 的情形。没有加拿大信用记录也很正常，用资金证明、在读证明和推荐信代替即可；在安省，没有信用记录本身不应该被当作扣分项。

## 人在国内，怎么安全"云看房"？

1. **要求实时视频看房**，不要只看对方发来的录像。请对方打开衣柜、开水龙头、拍窗外的景色，再走到门口拍一下街道。
2. **核实对方身份**：问清全名，确认他是业主或物业管理方。正规物业公司会有官网、办公地址和电话，可以自己打过去核实。
3. **请多伦多信得过的朋友**帮忙实地看一次。
4. **用地址和图片搜索一下**，骗子经常盗用真实房源的照片。
5. **拿不准就问学校住房办公室**，请老师帮你看看房源和租约。

## 中文找房渠道：方便，但更要小心

很多同学会在微信群、小红书、51.ca 和约克论坛上找房、找室友。这些渠道沟通方便、更新快，还能找到生活习惯相近的中国室友，但也是假房源、冒充房东、一房多租的重灾区，尤其是每年七八月开学季前。

几个底线：对方不肯视频、只催你转定金的，不要继续；价格明显低于同区域行情的，先打个问号；"学长学姐转租"要确认他是否有权转租、房东是否同意；聊天中途换账号、要求你换平台私聊付款的，都要警惕。

## 签订安省标准租约

安省大多数住宅租赁都必须使用政府的标准租约，上面写明房租、包含哪些费用、押金，以及双方必须遵守的规则。重点看"附加条款" (additional terms)：违反《住宅租赁法》的条款，即使你签了字也无效。

如果房东没给你标准租约，你可以书面要求；房东在 21 天内仍不提供的，安省规定给了你一些选择，在某些情况下可以暂扣最多一个月的房租。详细解读见 [安省标准租约](/zh/blog/ontario-standard-lease/)。

**重要例外**：如果你和房屋业主本人或其近亲共用厨房或卫生间，《住宅租赁法》一般不适用，标准租约也不适用。寄宿家庭 (homestay) 和部分"房东同住"的单间就属于这种情况，签约前一定问清楚。

## 押金和付款

在安省，房东可以收取：

- **租金押金**：不超过一个月房租，只能用来抵最后一个月房租；
- **可退还的钥匙押金**。

损坏押金是不允许的。房东每年要按当年涨租指导线给押金算利息（2026 年为 2.1%）。房东不能把预付几个月房租作为出租条件；如果你自己决定主动预付，也要在核实房东、签好租约之后再付，并拿到收据。

付款用可追踪的方式，比如 e-transfer 给已核实的房东，或支票；所有收据和聊天记录都要保存好。

## 专门针对留学生的骗局

留学生常常人在国外、时间紧，最容易成为目标。2026 年 6 月，多伦多警方通报在 Yonge 和 Finch 附近一宗涉嫌租房诈骗案中逮捕一名嫌疑人，受害者多为没看房就付了定金的国际学生。常见套路包括：

- **热门地段房租低得离谱**；
- **"我在国外，钥匙寄给你"**；
- **同一套房租给好几个人**，每人都交了定金；
- **假中介**还没看房就要护照、学签照片；
- **催你今天就付钱**，说"好多同学在抢"；
- **无权转租的人**把房子"转租"给你。

如果不幸遇到，马上联系银行，向多伦多警察局和加拿大反诈骗中心 (CAFC) 报案，并告诉学校住房办公室。更多防骗要点见 [多伦多租房防骗指南](/zh/blog/toronto-rental-scams/)。

## 用好学校的住房资源

- **多伦多大学**：Off-Campus Housing Finder 面向持 UTORid 的学生，还有找室友功能。
- **TMU**：Off-Campus Housing Office 为在读和即将入学的学生提供预约咨询和资源。
- **约克大学**：校外住房服务包括房源平台，以及租客和房东纠纷方面的支持。
- **各学院**：Humber、Seneca、Centennial、George Brown 等都有住房或学生事务团队可以求助。

这些服务都是免费的，老师们见过的骗局比你想象的多得多。

## 预算怎么做？

根据多大学生生活办公室 2026 年春季汇总的数据，多伦多一个房间的平均月租大约在 1,150 到 1,220 加元之间，市中心和学校附近通常更贵。除了房租，还要把水电网、租客保险、交通费、买菜和日用品都算进去。刚落地的第一个月开销最大：第一个月房租、最后一个月房租押金、短租过渡、买床垫和锅碗瓢盆，往往加起来是一笔不小的数目，建议提前多准备一些。具体拆解可以参考本站的《多伦多租房多少钱》一文。

另外，留学生在加拿大打工有工时等方面的限制，具体以你的学签条件和移民局 (IRCC) 的最新规定为准。做预算时不要把还没找到的兼职收入算进去，先用确定能到手的钱来规划房租。

## 搬进去之后

入住第一周做好下面几件小事，能省掉以后很多麻烦：

- **记录房屋状况**：给每个房间拍带日期的照片和视频，包括已有的损坏，并通过邮件发给房东留底。
- **买租客保险**：保障你的个人物品；万一你不小心造成漏水等损失，个人责任险也能派上用场。
- **开通水电网**：房租不包含的部分要自己开户，并确认每个账户登记在谁的名下。
- **保存房东联系方式**：问清楚报修流程，最好以书面形式沟通。
- **按时交房租、保留收据**：在这里留下良好的租房记录，下次租房时就是很有分量的推荐。

## 找到靠谱的室友

## 常见问题

**留学生应该提前多久在多伦多找房？**
想住学校宿舍的话，接受录取后尽快申请，截止日期往往在年初。校外租房的房源一般在入住前一到两个月才集中出现，部分原因是按月租住的租客搬走要提前 60 天通知房东。建议提前三四个月开始了解社区和预算，入住前六到八周开始集中找房。

**人还在国内，可以先在多伦多租好房子吗？**
可以，但风险更高。务必核实房东身份、要求实时视频看房，最好请在多伦多信得过的朋友实地看一次，签好书面租约后再付款。很多同学会先订两三周短租，落地实地看房后再签长租。

**留学生租房要准备哪些材料？**
房东通常会要护照、学签或入境前的签证批准信、在读证明或录取信、资金证明（如银行流水），有的话再加推荐信，有些房东还会要求担保人。租房不需要提供社会保险号 (SIN)。

**没看房就先付定金安全吗？**
这是留学生被骗最常见的情形之一。在确认对方确实是房东或物业管理方、并且实地或实时视频看过房之前，不要付任何钱。付款要用可追踪的方式，并保留收据。

**只租一个房间，也适用安省标准租约吗？**
如果你的租赁受《住宅租赁法》(RTA) 管辖，一般都适用。主要例外是你和房屋业主本人或其近亲共用厨房或卫生间，这时 RTA 和标准租约通常都不适用，你能得到的保护也更少。

**留学生租房遇到问题可以找谁？**
先找学校的住房办公室。多大有 Off-Campus Housing Finder，TMU 有 Off-Campus Housing Office，约克大学也有校外住房服务；各学院一般也有住房或学生事务老师，可以帮你看房源和租约。

## 参考资料

# Legal Basement Apartment Toronto: What to Check First

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/legal-basement-apartments-toronto/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-11-03

Renting a legal basement apartment in Toronto? Check exit windows, smoke and CO alarms, ceiling height and heat, and know the rights you keep if it isn't legal.

A legal basement apartment in Toronto is a second suite that's allowed by the City's zoning and built to meet the Ontario Building Code and Fire Code, usually with a building permit. Before you rent, check for a safe second way out, working smoke and carbon monoxide (CO) alarms, enough ceiling height and reliable heat. Even if a basement unit isn't fully legal, you're still protected by the Residential Tenancies Act (RTA) in most cases.

## Key takeaways

- Toronto zoning allows a **second suite** in most houses, but legal also means **built to code** with permits.
- **Safety first:** a second exit or large enough window, interconnected smoke alarms, and CO alarms where there's fuel-burning equipment.
- Your **RTA rights generally still apply** in a basement unit, legal or not, unless you share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner who lives there.
- A landlord **can't lock you out** because the unit isn't legal. Evictions go through the Landlord and Tenant Board (LTB).
- Report fire-safety problems to your landlord in writing, then to **311** if they aren't fixed.

*This is general information, not legal advice. For your situation, contact the Landlord and Tenant Board or a community legal clinic.*

## What "legal" means for a Toronto basement apartment

There are really two layers:

1. **Zoning: is a second suite allowed here?** The City of Toronto's zoning bylaw allows a secondary suite in most detached houses, semi-detached houses and townhouses across the city.
2. **Building and fire safety: was it built properly?** The suite needs to meet the Ontario Building Code and the Ontario Fire Code. Creating a new suite generally requires a building permit and inspections.

Plenty of basement units in Toronto were finished years ago without permits. They may be on a street where suites are allowed but still miss key safety features. That's why it's worth checking the unit itself, not just asking "is this legal?"

## Basement apartment checklist: what to look at during a viewing

Bring this list and your phone's flashlight. You don't need to be an inspector to spot the big issues.

### Getting out safely

- [ ] Is there a **separate entrance**, or a clear exit that doesn't go through the main unit?
- [ ] If there's only one door, is there a **bedroom window big enough to climb out of**? Building Code standards for exit windows commonly call for an opening of at least 0.35 m², with no side narrower than 380 mm. Ask the landlord to confirm it meets code.
- [ ] Can the window actually be opened from inside without tools? Is it blocked by bars, furniture or a deep window well?
- [ ] Is the path to the exit free of storage and clutter?

### Alarms

- [ ] Is there a **working smoke alarm** in the unit and outside the sleeping area? Ask the landlord to press the test button.
- [ ] In a house with two units, are the smoke alarms **interconnected**, so an alarm upstairs sounds downstairs too?
- [ ] Is there a **carbon monoxide alarm** near the bedrooms? Ontario requires CO alarms in homes with a fuel-burning appliance (such as a gas furnace or water heater), a fireplace or an attached garage.

### Space and comfort

- [ ] **Ceiling height:** can you stand comfortably everywhere? Secondary suites are allowed somewhat lower ceilings than a typical new home, roughly 1.95 m in main areas and a bit less under beams and ducts, but the exact rules depend on when and how the suite was built.
- [ ] **Heat:** does the unit have its own heat source or vents, and do you control the thermostat? Ask how warm it stays in January.
- [ ] **Moisture:** any musty smell, water stains, peeling paint or white crust on the walls? Check under sinks and in corners.
- [ ] **Light and air:** are there windows that open? Is there a bathroom fan that vents outside?
- [ ] **Furnace room:** is it separated from the living space with a door, rather than open to your bedroom?
- [ ] **Electrical:** are there enough outlets, or would you need extension cords everywhere?

### Paperwork and practical details

- [ ] Ask whether the suite was built with a **building permit** and passed inspection.
- [ ] Ask who pays **utilities** and whether your hydro is separate or shared with upstairs.
- [ ] Ask whether **laundry** is shared and when you can use it.
- [ ] Will you get the **Ontario Standard Lease**? Most residential tenancies in Ontario need one. See our guide to the [Ontario standard lease](/blog/ontario-standard-lease/).

### Questions to ask the landlord

1. Was this suite built with a building permit, and did it pass final inspection?
2. When were the smoke and CO alarms last tested or replaced?
3. Has the basement ever flooded or had water come in? What was done about it?
4. How is the unit heated, and is there air conditioning or a dehumidifier in summer?
5. Who lives upstairs, and do we share laundry, the entrance or the backyard?
6. Are utilities included, or split with the upstairs unit? How is the split calculated?

## Legal vs unpermitted: what's different for you?

| Question | Legal, permitted suite | Unpermitted suite |
|---|---|---|
| Does the RTA protect me? | Yes, in most cases | Generally yes, in most cases |
| Can the landlord evict me without the LTB? | No | No |
| Is the landlord responsible for maintenance and repairs? | Yes | Yes |
| Was safety checked by an inspector? | Yes, at the time it was built | Not necessarily |
| Could the City order changes or closure? | Unlikely | Possible, which can disrupt your tenancy |

The biggest practical risk with an unpermitted unit isn't your legal status. It's **safety**, and the chance that the City orders work or the unit stops being rented, forcing you to move on short notice.

## Your rights still apply in a basement unit

If you have your own kitchen and bathroom, the RTA generally covers you in a basement apartment, permitted or not. That means:

- your rent deposit can't be more than one month's rent,
- rent increases follow the provincial rules,
- the landlord must keep the unit in a good state of repair and meet health, safety and maintenance standards,
- the landlord must give proper written notice before entering, except in emergencies, and
- the landlord needs a valid notice and an LTB order to evict you if you don't leave voluntarily.

**One big exception:** if you share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner (or the owner's close family) who lives in the house, the RTA may not apply. Read our guide to [living with your landlord in Ontario](/blog/living-with-your-landlord-ontario/).

Also, don't stop paying rent because the unit has problems. Withholding rent can lead to an eviction application against you. Use the proper process instead.

## How to report a problem

1. **Tell your landlord in writing.** Email or text works. Describe the problem, add photos and ask for a repair date.
2. **For smoke or CO alarm problems,** the City of Toronto advises tenants to notify the landlord, and if the landlord doesn't act, to call **311** for a referral to Toronto Fire Services.
3. **For other maintenance or property standards issues** (heat, mould, pests, leaks), you can also contact **311**.
4. **Apply to the LTB.** If repairs aren't done, a tenant can file a maintenance application (Form T6). If the landlord harasses you or locks you out, Form T2 covers tenant rights issues.
5. **Emergencies:** if there's fire, smoke or a CO alarm going off, get out and call **911**.

## Rent with confidence

## FAQ

**Are basement apartments legal in Toronto?**
Yes, the City of Toronto's zoning allows second suites in most detached houses, semi-detached houses and townhouses. A suite also needs to meet the Ontario Building Code and Fire Code, and creating one generally requires a building permit. A basement can be allowed by zoning but still not be built to code.

**Do I have tenant rights if my basement apartment is illegal?**
In most cases, yes. The Residential Tenancies Act generally applies to a rental unit whether or not the suite was built with permits, unless an exemption applies, such as sharing a kitchen or bathroom with the owner who lives there. Your landlord still needs to follow the LTB process to end your tenancy.

**How do I know if a basement apartment is legal?**
Ask the landlord whether the suite was created with a building permit and passed inspection, and ask to see the paperwork. Also check the basics yourself: a second way out, working interconnected smoke alarms, CO alarms if there's a furnace or other fuel-burning appliance, and adequate heat and ceiling height.

**Who do I call about fire safety problems in my Toronto basement unit?**
Tell your landlord in writing first. If smoke or CO alarms aren't fixed, call 311, which can refer the issue to Toronto Fire Services for inspection. Call 911 if there's smoke, fire or a CO alarm sounding.

**Can my landlord evict me because the basement isn't legal?**
Your landlord can't simply change the locks or tell you to leave. To end a tenancy covered by the RTA, they need a valid notice and, if you don't leave, an order from the Landlord and Tenant Board. Get advice quickly if this happens.

## Sources

- [City of Toronto: Overview of secondary suites](https://www.toronto.ca/city-government/planning-development/planning-studies-initiatives/secondary-suites/overview-secondary-suites/)
- [City of Toronto: Smoke alarms](https://www.toronto.ca/community-people/public-safety-alerts/safety-tips-prevention/safety-equipment-devices/smoke-alarms/)
- [City of Toronto: Carbon monoxide alarms](https://www.toronto.ca/community-people/public-safety-alerts/safety-tips-prevention/safety-equipment-devices/carbon-monoxide-alarms/)
- [Ontario: Carbon monoxide safety](https://www.ontario.ca/cosafety)
- [Residential Tenancies Act, 2006](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17)
- [Landlord and Tenant Board](https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/)

# 多伦多地下室租房：合法吗？看房必查清单

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/legal-basement-apartments-toronto/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-11-03

多伦多地下室租房便宜，但安全最要紧：层高、逃生窗、烟雾和一氧化碳报警器、暖气怎么查？没有许可的地下室，租客权益还在吗？看房前请收好这份实用清单。

多伦多地下室租房，所谓"合法地下室"，是指市政分区规定允许设立、并且按照安省建筑规范 (Ontario Building Code) 和消防规范 (Fire Code) 建造的附属单元 (second suite)，通常需要建筑许可。看房时最要紧的是：有没有安全的第二出口、烟雾和一氧化碳报警器是否正常、层高和暖气够不够。即使地下室不完全合法，大多数情况下你仍然受住宅租赁法 (RTA) 保护。

对刚落地的留学生和新移民来说，地下室常常是预算内最现实的选择：价格比楼上低、离地铁站和学校近、有时还有独立入口。但地下室的安全问题也最多，下面这份清单建议收藏，看房时逐项对照。

## 要点速览

- 多伦多允许大部分住宅设一个**附属单元**，但"合法"还要**按规范建造**、有许可。
- **安全第一**：第二出口或足够大的逃生窗、联动烟雾报警器、有燃气设备时必须有一氧化碳报警器。
- 地下室无论合不合法，**RTA一般都保护你**；例外是和住在家里的房东共用厨房或卫生间。
- 房东**不能因为地下室不合法就换锁赶人**，必须走房东租客委员会 (LTB) 程序。
- 安全问题先书面通知房东，没有解决就打**311**。

*本文仅为一般信息，不构成法律意见；具体情况请咨询房东租客委员会 (LTB) 或社区法律援助诊所 (community legal clinic)。*

## 多伦多地下室怎样才算"合法"？

其实分两层：

1. **分区 (zoning)：这里允许设附属单元吗？** 多伦多市的分区条例允许全市大部分独立屋、半独立屋和镇屋设一个附属单元。
2. **建筑和消防：是不是按规范建的？** 附属单元需要符合安省建筑规范和消防规范，新建一般需要申请建筑许可 (building permit) 并通过检查。

很多多伦多老房子的地下室是多年前自己装修的，没有许可。它所在的街道也许允许设附属单元，但安全设施可能不达标。所以，与其只问"合不合法"，不如亲自把下面这些项目检查一遍。

## 多伦多地下室看房必查清单

带上这份清单和手机手电筒，不需要专业知识也能发现大问题。

### 逃生出口

- [ ] 有没有**独立入口**，或者不需要经过楼上住户就能出去的出口？
- [ ] 如果只有一扇门，卧室里有没有**能爬出去的窗户**？建筑规范对逃生窗常见的要求是开口面积不小于0.35平方米、任何一边不窄于380毫米，可以请房东确认是否达标。
- [ ] 窗户能不能从里面徒手打开？有没有被防盗栏、家具或很深的窗井挡住？
- [ ] 通往出口的路上有没有堆杂物？

### 报警器

- [ ] 单元内、卧室外面有没有**能正常工作的烟雾报警器**？请房东当场按测试键。
- [ ] 楼上楼下两个单元的烟雾报警器是否**联动**（楼上响，楼下也会响）？
- [ ] 卧室附近有没有**一氧化碳报警器** (CO alarm)？安省规定，家里有燃气炉、燃气热水器等燃料设备、壁炉或连体车库的，必须安装一氧化碳报警器。

### 空间和舒适度

- [ ] **层高**：能不能到处都舒服地站直？附属单元允许的层高比一般新房低一些，主要区域大约1.95米，横梁和风管下方还可以更低，具体要求取决于建造时间和方式。
- [ ] **暖气**：单元有没有独立暖气或出风口？温度能不能自己调？问问房东一月份屋里有多暖。
- [ ] **潮湿**：有没有霉味、水渍、墙皮脱落、墙上白色结晶？看看水槽下面和墙角。
- [ ] **采光通风**：有没有能打开的窗？卫生间的排风扇是否通向室外？
- [ ] **锅炉房**：炉子所在房间有没有门和居住空间隔开？
- [ ] **电路**：插座够不够用？会不会到处拉接线板？

### 文件和生活细节

- [ ] 问清楚这个单元有没有**建筑许可**、是否通过检查。
- [ ] **水电网**谁付？电表是独立的，还是和楼上共用分摊？
- [ ] **洗衣机**是否共用？什么时间可以用？
- [ ] 会不会签**安省标准租约** (Ontario Standard Lease)？安省大多数住宅租赁都需要使用，详见[安省标准租约指南](/zh/blog/ontario-standard-lease/)。

### 看房时可以直接问房东的问题

1. 这个单元有没有建筑许可？最后有没有通过检查？
2. 烟雾报警器和一氧化碳报警器最近一次测试或更换是什么时候？
3. 地下室以前有没有进过水、淹过？后来怎么处理的？
4. 冬天靠什么供暖？夏天有没有空调或除湿机？
5. 楼上住的是谁？洗衣机、入口、后院是否共用？
6. 水电是包在房租里，还是和楼上分摊？怎么算？

### 冬天和雨季要特别留意

多伦多冬天漫长寒冷，地下室贴近地面，保暖和防潮尤其重要。看房最好选在白天，留意光线；如果是夏天看房，记得问冬天的室温和暖气情况。春季融雪和夏季暴雨时，地下室比较容易进水，可以看看地面和墙角有没有水渍、地毯有没有发霉的痕迹，问问房东有没有排水泵 (sump pump)。如果你有很多电子设备或重要证件，不要直接放在地上。买一份租客保险 (tenant insurance)，问清楚是否包含水浸损失，也能多一层保障。

## 地下室租房的优点和缺点

| | 优点 | 缺点 |
|---|---|---|
| 价格 | 通常比同区域的楼上单元便宜 | 便宜得离谱的要警惕安全或诈骗问题 |
| 隐私 | 常有独立入口，不用和房东碰面 | 楼上脚步声、说话声可能比较明显 |
| 位置 | 很多在成熟社区，靠近地铁和学校 | 部分老房子离公共交通较远 |
| 舒适度 | 夏天相对凉快 | 采光较少，冬季和雨季容易潮湿 |
| 安全 | 按规范建造的单元有逃生出口和联动报警器 | 无许可单元未必经过检查 |

总的来说，地下室并不等于"差房子"。只要安全设施到位、房东负责，很多同学和新移民在地下室住得很舒服，还省下不少房租。关键是看房时不怕麻烦，多看、多问、多拍照。

## 合法 vs 无许可地下室：对你有什么不同？

| 问题 | 有许可的合法单元 | 无许可单元 |
|---|---|---|
| 受RTA保护吗？ | 大多数情况受保护 | 一般也受保护 |
| 房东能不经LTB赶人吗？ | 不能 | 不能 |
| 房东要负责维修吗？ | 要 | 要 |
| 安全有没有人检查过？ | 建造时检查过 | 不一定 |
| 市政府会不会要求整改或停用？ | 可能性小 | 有可能，会打乱你的租住计划 |

无许可地下室最大的风险其实不是法律身份，而是**安全**，以及市政府要求整改、单元不能再出租时，你可能要临时搬家。

## 住地下室，你的权利一样在

只要你有独立的厨房和卫生间，无论有没有许可，RTA一般都适用：

- 押金不能超过一个月租金；
- 涨租要遵守省政府的规定；
- 房东必须保持房屋良好维修状态，符合健康、安全和维护标准；
- 除紧急情况外，房东进门前必须提前书面通知；
- 你不愿意搬走时，房东需要合法通知加LTB的命令才能驱逐你。

**重要例外：** 如果你和住在家里的房东（或其近亲）共用厨房或卫生间，RTA可能不适用，详见[和房东同住：安省租房指南](/zh/blog/living-with-your-landlord-ontario/)。

另外，千万不要因为房子有问题就自行停交房租。扣租可能让房东反过来向LTB申请驱逐你，应该走正规流程。

## 入住后，自己也要做好的几件事

- 每个月按一次烟雾报警器和一氧化碳报警器的测试键，听到"滴滴"的低电提示要马上告诉房东；
- 不要拆掉报警器的电池，也不要用东西把报警器罩住，做饭油烟大就开窗、开抽油烟机；
- 逃生窗前不要堆放箱子和家具，保证随时能打开；
- 电暖器远离窗帘和床单，不用的时候关掉；
- 和室友约好着火时在屋外哪里集合。

## 遇到问题，怎么投诉？

1. **书面通知房东。** 邮件或短信都行，写清问题、附上照片，并要求给出维修时间。
2. **烟雾或一氧化碳报警器的问题**：多伦多市建议先通知房东；房东不处理的，打**311**，会转介给多伦多消防局 (Toronto Fire Services)。
3. **暖气、发霉、虫害、漏水等维护问题**：也可以联系**311**。
4. **向LTB申请。** 维修一直不做，租客可以提交T6表格（维护问题）；被骚扰或被锁在门外，可以用T2表格（租客权益问题）。
5. **紧急情况**：着火、冒烟或一氧化碳报警器响，立刻离开并拨打**911**。

## 安心租好每一间地下室

## 常见问题

**多伦多的地下室公寓合法吗？**
多伦多市的分区规定 (zoning) 允许大部分独立屋、半独立屋和镇屋设一个附属单元 (second suite)。但合法还要求符合安省建筑规范 (Building Code) 和消防规范 (Fire Code)，新建通常需要建筑许可。分区允许，不代表这套地下室一定按规范建造。

**地下室不合法，我还受租客法保护吗？**
大多数情况下仍受保护。住宅租赁法 (RTA) 一般适用于出租单元，不管它有没有建筑许可；例外是你和住在家里的房东共用厨房或卫生间。房东要终止租约，仍须走LTB的程序。

**怎么判断地下室是不是合法的？**
直接问房东这个单元是否有建筑许可 (building permit)、是否通过检查，并请对方出示文件。同时自己检查：有没有第二个出口、烟雾报警器是否联动、有燃气炉等设备时有没有一氧化碳报警器、暖气和层高是否够。

**地下室报警器坏了房东不修，找谁？**
先书面通知房东。如果烟雾或一氧化碳报警器的问题没有解决，可以打311，市政府会转介给多伦多消防局 (Toronto Fire Services) 检查。有烟、火或一氧化碳报警响起时，立即离开并拨打911。

## 参考资料

- [City of Toronto: Overview of secondary suites](https://www.toronto.ca/city-government/planning-development/planning-studies-initiatives/secondary-suites/overview-secondary-suites/)
- [City of Toronto: Smoke alarms](https://www.toronto.ca/community-people/public-safety-alerts/safety-tips-prevention/safety-equipment-devices/smoke-alarms/)
- [City of Toronto: Carbon monoxide alarms](https://www.toronto.ca/community-people/public-safety-alerts/safety-tips-prevention/safety-equipment-devices/carbon-monoxide-alarms/)
- [Ontario: Carbon monoxide safety](https://www.ontario.ca/cosafety)
- [Residential Tenancies Act, 2006](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17)
- [Landlord and Tenant Board](https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/)
